description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4, `comp/` CHECK 2).  PRE-EXISTING.

perl's `@INC` may hold a CODE ref, an ARRAY ref whose first element is one, or
an object with an `INC` method (perldoc -f require).  The hook is called with
(itself, the filename) and may return: nothing (skip this hook), a filehandle,
a CODE ref that is called repeatedly to yield source lines in `$_`, or a
[coderef, state] pair.  It is how `Filter::Util::Call`, `Devel::` loaders and
several test harnesses get their source in.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

    BEGIN { unshift @INC, sub {
        return () unless $_[1] =~ m{\AHookMe\.pm\z};
        my $done = 0;
        return sub { return 0 if $done;
                     $_ = "package HookMe; sub hi { 'HI' } 1;\n";
                     $done = 1; return 1 };
    } }
    my $r = eval { require "HookMe.pm" };
    print "rv=[", (defined $r ? $r : 'undef'), "] err=[$@]\n";
    print "hi=[", (HookMe->can('hi') ? HookMe::hi() : 'no-sub'), "]\n";

    perl:  rv=[1] err=[]          hi=[HI]
    PCL :  rv=[undef]  err=[The value #<function (lambda (&rest %_args) ...)>
                            is not of type
                            (or string pathname synonym-stream file-stream)
                            when binding pathname at (eval 0) line 0.]
           hi=[no-sub]

TWO FAULTS, and the second is the one that makes it a rule-12 item:
  (a) the feature is absent -- an @INC entry that is not a string is not
      recognised as a hook;
  (b) the absence is SILENT in the sense rule 12 forbids: the non-string entry
      flows into the host's `open`, and SBCL's type error becomes the perl
      program's `$@`.  A caller that tests `$@` against a pattern sees a
      plausible-looking string that names none of this.  The minimum fix, even
      without the feature, is to DIE perl-shaped at the point where an @INC
      entry is not a string -- "PCL: unsupported: a CODE ref in @INC ..." --
      or, since require then falls through to the remaining @INC entries in
      perl, to SKIP a non-string entry and announce on stderr (the s329
      effect-only boundary; a skip is what perl does for a hook that returns
      nothing).

WHAT IT COSTS: t/comp/filter_exception.t DIFF 2/2 -- rows 2 and 4, both
`like $@, qr/\AToo many arguments for int /`.  Row 4 is where the SBCL text
shows up; row 2 fails for the separate reason that PCL does not produce
compile-time arity errors for builtins at all (NS:Error compatibility for
invalid Perl input).  t/op/incfilter.t's 153 rows are the same feature but
gated behind `Filter::Util::Call` being XS (already cited as NS:Source
filters in `baselines/row-shortfall.tsv`), so this task's own prize is 1 row
plus the leak.

LAYER (CLAUDE.md 9a): the hook PROTOCOL is perl core -- `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`'s
`p-require-file` -- and nothing about it names a module.  `Filter::Util::Call`
itself is a shim question and stays out.
subject: A CODE ref in @INC (perl's require hook) is handed to the pathname binding, so `require` leaks a raw SBCL type error into $@ instead of calling the hook -- rule 12's silence, and t/comp/filter_exception.t's 2 rows
